fixes.where: intro and agreed summary and terms (mode of baptism)
fixes.why: The card calls the mode of baptism 'a smaller question' in the intro and the agreed summary, and the mode term note says 'the churches treat the question as smaller than who is baptized and what baptism does'. That is a weighting verdict. Immersion is required practice for the Orthodox and for Baptists, and the burial reading of Romans 6:4 carries the Baptist and Anabaptist case.
fixes.fix: Intro: replace 'and, as a smaller question, on how the water is applied' with 'and, on a separate question, on how the water is applied'. Agreed summary: replace 'and, as a smaller question, over whether the water is poured or the person immersed' with 'and, on a separate question, over whether the water is poured or the person immersed'. Mode of baptism term note: delete the sentence 'The range of the Greek verb baptizō is part of the discussion, and the churches treat the question as smaller than who is baptized and what baptism does.' and put in its place: 'Churches differ on this question too, and each reading's summary says which mode its holders use.'

fixes.why: The definition 'the washing with water by which ... are received in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit' gives the threefold formula as the definition and says baptism receives people, which is the sense of the first reading. Acts 2:38, quoted under the first and third readings, names Jesus Christ alone. The definition should not decide which formula or which effect the page starts from.
fixes.fix: Replace the first sentence of the intro with: 'Baptism is the rite with water in which Christ's followers are baptized, in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19) or in the name of Jesus Christ (Acts 2:38).' Keep the rest of the intro, changing only 'and, as a smaller question, on how the water is applied' as in fix 1.

fixes.why: 'baptism joins the one baptized to Christ' is stated as common ground, but the third reading's holders take baptism to picture union with Christ's death (Romans 6:4) and do not say it joins. The agreed block has to be common to every reading below it.
fixes.fix: Replace 'and that baptism joins the one baptized to Christ, including his death' with 'and that those baptized are baptized into Christ and into his death, as Romans 6:3 says'.

fixes.where: agreed summary and third reading summary
fixes.why: The agreed block says every reading takes the text to say that baptism is in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Oneness Pentecostal bodies, which fall under the Pentecostal holders of the third reading, baptize in the name of Jesus alone on Acts 2:38, so the common ground is not common to them. The _why calls this a separate question, but the card's own statement is what a Pentecostal reader would check.
fixes.fix: Agreed summary: after 'in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit' insert ', as Matthew 28:19 has it (Oneness Pentecostal bodies, noted under the third reading, baptize in the name of Jesus alone)'. Third reading summary: after 'Pentecostal churches share this practice' insert 'and Oneness Pentecostal bodies baptize in the name of Jesus alone, on Acts 2:38'.

fixes.where: second reading (label 'Baptism as the sign and seal of God's covenant promise...') summary, and first reading held_by and summary
fixes.why: The second reading places Wesleyan / Methodist only under covenant sign, with 'differing accounts of what baptism itself gives'. The Methodist Articles of Religion (Article XVII) call baptism a sign of regeneration or new birth, which is the language of the first reading. A Wesleyan reader would find the card places the tradition in one reading only and so misstates its position.
fixes.fix: First reading held_by: add 'Wesleyan / Methodist' to the list. First reading summary: after 'Anglican members hold this reading in varying measure.' insert 'Wesleyan and Methodist members hold it in part: the Methodist Articles of Religion (Article XVII) call baptism a sign of regeneration or new birth.' Second reading summary: replace 'Wesleyan and Methodist members baptize infants as a sign of God's grace toward children, with differing accounts of what baptism itself gives.' with 'Wesleyan and Methodist members baptize infants as a sign of God's grace toward children, and some hold the first reading as well.' (Wesleyan seat: confirm the article wording before shipping.)

fixes.why: 'the name means those who baptize again' is the gloss of the opponents who gave the name. Anabaptists hold that the infant sprinkling they were baptized in was not baptism, so the card's gloss frames their practice from outside it.
fixes.fix: Replace '(the name means those who baptize again, from the sixteenth-century practice of baptizing those who were baptized as infants)' with '(a name given by their opponents in the sixteenth century, meaning those who baptize again; they hold that the infant sprinkling they had received was not baptism)'.

fixes.why: The note says the site marks the verse as absent from the earliest manuscripts, and stops there. The verse is quoted by holders who read the longer ending as Scripture, and the note as written leaves the verse looking doubtful to them without saying so. The mark is the site's rule and stays.
fixes.fix: Replace the note with: 'The site marks Mark 16:9-20 as absent from the earliest manuscripts, which end Mark after verse 8; the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and Lutheran churches read the longer ending as Scripture.'

fixes.why: 'Baptism in the Spirit' is named in the terms list with Acts 1:5 and 1 Corinthians 12:13, but the third reading, which Pentecostal holders take, never answers the verse they cite first for that distinction. Acts 1:5 and Acts 19:5 are the two verses this distinction rests on; neither is in the reading's answers. Acts 1:5 is confirmed against the Berean text; 1 Corinthians 12:13 was not re-read here.
fixes.fix: Append to the third reading's 'answers' field: 'Holders who distinguish baptism in the Spirit from baptism in water take Acts 1:5, "For John baptized with water, but in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit," as the promise of that baptism, and Acts 19:5, "On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus," as baptism that follows hearing.' Passage count stays at 8.

summary: The card is structured fairly and every one of its 28 quotes matches the Berean exactly, so the fixes are about wording and a few held_by and answer gaps rather than the text itself. The main risks are that the card ranks the mode of baptism as a smaller question and that its definition and agreed block assume views that the Baptist, Anabaptist and Oneness Pentecostal holders do not share.
